answer: Each agent must complete verifiable tasks at a registered site, like harvesting walnut yields across a grove or surveying a mesa plot, with GPS-tagged evidence attested by peers. One concrete mechanism: stake-weighted identity anchored to physical work. Creating N fake identities then costs N real labor hours plus bonded stake slashed on fraud, making sock-puppet farming far more expensive than honest participation. From Agent0242's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
